A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDIM-GMM research work. All 29 pages of v3 and 34 pages of v5, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison; v5 substantially extends the work.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation evaluations with FID and IS scores, sampler comparisons, parameter ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds rectified-flow evaluations, expanded ablations, runtime measurements and text-to-image examples.

M1.justification: v5 introduces RFIM and RFIM-GMM sampling procedures for rectified-flow models in Sections 4–4.1, including stochastic transition kernels and adaptations of the three GMM variants. These extend the procedure beyond v3's diffusion/DDIM setting; the original DDIM-GMM constructions remain.

E1.justification: v5 adds CIFAR-10 image-generation evaluation and an ImageNet64 setting. CelebAHQ, FFHQ, ImageNet256, COYO-700M and LSUN Bedroom/Church remain, making this a limited expansion within the existing image-generation coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Tables 1–2 introduce unimodal RFIM, including its stated deterministic Euler case, as a comparator for RFIM-GMM. Comparator membership in the retained DDIM, DDPM and DPM-Solver comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 introduces rectified-flow evaluations using 50,000 generated samples, eta values of 0, 0.2 and 0.5, and distinct sampling-step budgets for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet64. It also expands the ablation scale search to include 20 and adds a 100-sample timing protocol. These are additions or revisions to evaluation design, without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 Section 4.5 studies component count and offset scale only for ORTHO-VUB. v5 Appendix A.8 extends both analyses to RAND and ORTHO and tests the larger scale 20; Appendix A.10 adds measured computational overhead. The parameter-sharing analysis is retained in Appendix A.9 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, independent repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. v5 averages timing over 100 generated samples, but this specifies the new timing experiment's sample size and does not introduce between-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All ten v3 tables retain their numerical contents in v5 Tables 3 and 5–13. v5 adds substantial results for rectified-flow sampling, expanded ablations and runtime. For example, Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 FID of 6.37 for RFIM versus 6.13 for ORTHO/ORTHO-VUB at 50 steps and eta=0. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over corresponding v3 measurements.

T1.justification: v5 adds rectified-flow interpolant and loss definitions, the RFIM transition kernel, variance constraints, an asserted Euler limit and a multimodality derivation in Eqs. 15–22. The original appendix proofs are largely retained. The new Eq. 20, as printed, has a plus sign inconsistent with the marginal mean in Eq. 18 and the claimed Euler limit.

C1.justification: v5 retains the original DDIM moment-matching and few-step generation claims, while adding a fourth contribution: novel stochastic solvers for rectified-flow models and improvements using their GMM extensions. This broadens the abstract, introduction and conclusion beyond v3's diffusion-sampling contribution.

C2.justification: v5 refines the existing exploration/stability interpretation by distinguishing the effects of scale 20 across RAND, ORTHO and ORTHO-VUB. Section 5.4 additionally attributes RFIM-GMM gains to offset stochasticity and explains poorer high-eta sampling through reduced dependence along the sampling chain.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-code link, identifies UNet/OT-CFM training for CIFAR-10 and the source of the ImageNet64 checkpoint, and documents V100 32GB hardware and timing procedures. The original architecture, noise-schedule and variance-clipping details in Appendix A.5 remain.

R1.justification: v5 substantially extends positioning to stochastic rectified-flow solvers through stochastic interpolants and DDIM/Euler equivalence. It also adds consistency-model and newer distillation references. Several flow-related works were already listed in v3's bibliography; the substantive change is their developed relationship to the new contribution.

P1.justification: Most retained prose remains similar. v5 inserts the RFIM sections, moves parameter sharing and ablations from the main text into Appendices A.9 and A.8, expands the forward-process notation, updates affiliation/publication text and repairs the acknowledgments heading.

P2.justification: v3's combined eight-panel ablation Figure 5 becomes two twelve-panel figures in v5, organized by sampler variant. v5 adds two rectified-flow tables, a runtime table and a text-to-image comparison figure, relocates the parameter-sharing table, and rearranges retained appendix tables.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens practical evidence through broader ablations, measured overhead, new evaluations and a code pointer. However, its new central RFIM derivation is internally inconsistent: Eq. 20 does not preserve Eq. 18's mean or recover the claimed Euler limit as printed. The PDFs do not establish whether this is confined to the equation or affects the implemented sampler. These benefits and the unresolved theoretical defect prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
